scope: Private commercial projects; first-tier subcontractor contracting with the general (prime/original) contractor.
verification: Checked 2026-10-25 against statute text quoted from the official legislature domains below (via search excerpts; full-page reads were not possible from the build sandbox). Needs a full read of each official page and attorney review before launch.

rules.title: Preliminary 20-day notice
rules.note: Serve the owner, the direct contractor and any construction lender within 20 days after you first furnish work. A late notice still protects work furnished in the 20 days before it is served, and after.

rules.title: Record mechanics lien
rules.note: The statute allows recording after you stop work and before the earlier of 90 days after completion of the whole project or 30 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation. LienClock counts 90 days from your last furnishing date, which is never later than completion. If a notice of completion is recorded, your real deadline can be earlier than shown.

rules.title: Notice of claim for unpaid work
rules.note: For each month in which you furnished labor or materials that are still unpaid, send notice to the owner and the original contractor by the 15th day of the third month after that month. A missed month loses lien rights for that month. Applies to original contracts dated on or after 2022-01-01. The statute moves a deadline that falls on a weekend or legal holiday to the next business day; LienClock shows the unextended date.

rules.title: File lien affidavit
rules.note: File with the county clerk by the 15th day of the fourth month after the month you last furnished labor or materials, and send a copy to the owner and original contractor. Retainage claims have their own deadlines (§ 53.057, § 53.052(d)) that LienClock does not track yet. Weekend and holiday deadlines roll forward under the statute; LienClock shows the unextended date.

rules.title: Notice to Owner
rules.note: Serve the owner (and the contractor) before you start or within 45 days after you start furnishing, and in any case before the owner makes final payment. A late or missing notice is a complete defense to your lien.

rules.title: Record claim of lien
rules.note: Record within 90 days after your final furnishing. If the original contract is terminated, the deadline is 90 days after termination when that is earlier.

rules.title: Record claim of lien
rules.note: Record within 90 days after you stop furnishing labor, materials or equipment, and give the owner a copy within 14 days of recording. A subcontractor contracting directly with the prime contractor on a commercial job needs no preliminary notice (RCW 60.04.031(2)(c)).

rules.title: Preliminary 20-day notice
rules.note: Serve within 20 days after you first furnish labor or materials. A late notice still protects work furnished in the 20 days before it is served, and after.

rules.title: Record mechanics lien
rules.note: The statute counts 120 days from completion of the whole project, or 60 days after a notice of completion is recorded. LienClock counts 120 days from your last furnishing date, which is never later than completion. If a notice of completion is recorded, your real deadline can be earlier than shown.

rules.title: Notice of right to lien
rules.note: Deliver in person or by certified mail to the owner, with a copy to the prime contractor. It protects work furnished in the 31 days before it is given, and after, so give it within 31 days of first furnishing to cover everything.

rules.title: Record notice of lien
rules.note: The statute counts 90 days from the latest of project completion or your last work or delivery, or 40 days after a recorded notice of completion. LienClock counts from your last furnishing date, which is never later. Serve the owner within 30 days of recording.
